items.title: Predicting Pain: Electroencephalography Signatures of Neural Integration During Experimental Tonic Thermal Pain
items.authors: Yiyuan Han, Elia Valentini, Sebastian Halder
items.feature_family: Alpha inter-site phase connectivity (ISPC); phase-based cross-frequency coupling (delta/theta/alpha/low beta); dwPLI robustness analysis
items.feature_definition: ISPC is mean phase-difference consistency across channels or frequency bands; dwPLI weights non-zero-lag phase coupling.
items.prediction_rationale: Authors found phase features more discriminative than power features for tonic thermal pain; proposed use is within-person pain/non-pain state classification, not continuous pain-rating prediction.
items.verified_result_metric: Phase features outperformed power features; abstract calls accuracy high but numeric accuracy not verified in saved evidence.
items.prediction_target: Tonic thermal pain versus non-painful warm/rest conditions
items.validation_design: Within-participant binary comparisons; separate temporal halves for feature selection and evaluation, swapped; 10-fold CV on evaluation half. Overlapping epochs handled by temporal-half split.
items.data_evidence: Article-linked OSF EEG-data URL found in a research-result record, but fetched OSF page showed sign-in and raw file access/content was not independently verified; do not count as verified public raw EEG.
items.relevance_limitations: Study used 62 channels, 1000-Hz acquisition and frontal/occipital topographies; strongest coupling was low-frequency. Pipeline C3/C4/Cz only misses frontal/occipital topology. Reproduce original bands (to low beta) within 1–40 Hz; check event/rest condition timing and 1–10-s windows. Source compares state labels, not pain severity ratings.

items.title: Exploring electroencephalographic chronic pain biomarkers: a mega-analysis
items.feature_family: Resting-state EEG large-scale brain-network connectivity (metric family; not PLV/PLI/wPLI/PAC specifically verified in saved evidence)
items.feature_definition: Connectivity among large-scale functional brain networks; study includes frequency-specific network analyses.
items.prediction_rationale: Pain-intensity-associated network connectivity can motivate participant-level severity modelling, but the source reports association analysis, not a validated prediction tool.
items.verified_result_metric: Discovery/replication associations had limited replicability; pooled mega-analysis found pain-intensity associations at theta and limbic-including networks; no numeric predictive R²/correlation verified in saved abstract.
items.prediction_target: Chronic pain intensity association (not a confirmed out-of-sample prediction target)
items.validation_design: Discovery–replication followed by mega-analysis across eight independent resting EEG datasets; 614 people with chronic pain.
items.data_evidence: Methods report contacting study authors and receiving datasets from four external groups; captured evidence did not verify a public raw-EEG repository or participant-level download.
items.relevance_limitations: Resting-state large-scale network coverage exceeds C3/C4/Cz. Avoid treating the pooled associations as predictive performance; check frequency definition and epoch length before transfer. No public-data criterion satisfied from current evidence.

items.title: Resting-state frontal electroencephalography (EEG) biomarkers for detecting the severity of chronic neuropathic pain
items.authors: S. Ryu, D. Gwon, C. Park, Y. Ha, M. Ahn
items.feature_family: Frontal EEG PAC and PAC asymmetry; spectral power asymmetry
items.feature_definition: Cross-frequency coupling between low-frequency phase and higher-frequency amplitude at Fp1/Fp2; left-right asymmetry features.
items.prediction_rationale: PAC/asymmetry may capture chronic pain severity-related nonstationary interactions missed by band power; this rationale is directly tested by the paper’s correlations and regression models.
items.verified_result_metric: Reported r: beta-power asymmetry −0.375; gamma-power asymmetry −0.433; low-beta-to-low-gamma coupling −0.397. Best polynomial-kernel SVR R²=0.655; no external validation verified.
items.prediction_target: Patient-level chronic neuropathic pain intensity from clinical ratings
items.validation_design: Secondary analysis of public resting EEG from 36 patients; feature-score correlations and five-model regression comparison; no external cohort/independent-site validation reported in retrieved abstract.
items.data_evidence: Ryu methods explicitly identify a publicly available dataset from the cited Zolezzi study; the linked 2023 data paper reports raw resting EEG plus BPI/painDETECT reports and Mendeley repository DOI 10.17632/yj52xrfgtz.4.
items.relevance_limitations: The actual predictor channels are Fp1/Fp2, absent in C3/C4/Cz pipeline; frontal asymmetry cannot be recreated. Resting 5-min eyes-open data and person-level pain labels differ from five-second trial labels. Gamma feature bands may exceed 40 Hz; any >64-Hz high-gamma component is beyond 128-Hz Nyquist and current filter.

items.title: Chronic neuropathic pain: EEG data in eyes open and eyes closed with painDETECT and brief pain inventory reports
items.authors: Daniela M. Zolezzi, Norberto E. Naal-Ruiz, Luz María Alonso-Valerdi, David I. Ibarra-Zarate
items.feature_family: Public resting EEG resource for candidate PAC, phase connectivity and feature-stability analyses
items.feature_definition: Raw 250-Hz EEG from 36 chronic neuropathic-pain patients (5-min eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions) with BPI and painDETECT questionnaires; paper reports bandwidth 0.1–100 Hz.
items.prediction_rationale: Could test whether within-session phase/PAC summaries carry information about patient questionnaire pain scores; this is a proposed reanalysis, not a result of the data descriptor.
items.verified_result_metric: Not applicable (dataset item; no prediction result claimed).
items.prediction_target: Proposed patient-level BPI/painDETECT severity or questionnaire-defined pain features
items.validation_design: Dataset includes 36 patients; analyses need subject-level splits to avoid window-level leakage and independent validation before clinical claims.
items.data_evidence: The data article links Mendeley repository versions and identifies raw electrophysiological signals plus questionnaire/demographic files; repository metadata identifies original data and files.
items.relevance_limitations: Resting state, not stimulus-locked pain; only 36 patients; five-second window labels would replicate a subject’s fixed clinical scores and are not independent. Verify channel layout for network connectivity; >40-Hz analyses require changing pipeline filters, and >64-Hz content is unavailable at 250-Hz sampling.

items.title: A comprehensive EEG dataset of laser-evoked potentials for pain research
items.feature_family: Public high-density stimulus-evoked EEG with single-trial pain ratings; candidate event-locked phase connectivity/CFC reanalysis
items.feature_definition: EEG from 678 healthy participants exposed to laser stimuli (2.5–4.5 J), with single-trial self-reported pain ratings embedded in EEGLAB epoch metadata; article links code/data repository.
items.prediction_rationale: Event-aligned inter-channel phase consistency or phase-amplitude coupling could be tested against trial-level pain ratings; proposed analysis, not a source-reported coupling result.
items.verified_result_metric: Not applicable (dataset item; no phase-feature prediction metric claimed).
items.prediction_target: Single-trial pain rating and/or pain discriminability after laser stimuli
items.validation_design: Large 678-participant resource; recommended subject-held-out validation and preserve event/condition grouping. Exact baseline/event intervals must be checked in event metadata before modeling.
items.open_access_status: Open-access data descriptor (PMC; explicit public-sharing consent)
items.data_evidence: Article describes high-density EEG and single-trial ratings, states participants consented to public data sharing, and links the repository containing dataset files and MATLAB code; its instructions point to EEG.epoch ratings.
items.relevance_limitations: Task-evoked laser responses require stimulus-marker and baseline timing rather than generic resting five-second epochs; verify event layout and electrode coverage. Sensor sampling/bandwidth must be checked before >40-Hz or >64-Hz features. Three central channels cannot reproduce high-density network maps.

items.title: Accurate classification of pain experiences using wearable electroencephalography in adolescents with and without chronic musculoskeletal pain
items.feature_family: Directed PLI (dPLI) and wPLI were calculated; only dPLI was retained in reported classification feature set; other entropy/graph features were also tested
items.feature_definition: wPLI summarizes weighted non-zero-lag phase coupling; dPLI captures direction of phase leads/lags. Paper reports wPLI removed before classification; dPLI retained.
items.prediction_rationale: dPLI’s reported classification performance is relevant to directional phase-based connectivity; it does not establish predictive utility for wPLI.
items.verified_result_metric: Separate SVM baseline-vs-CPT classification: chronic-pain cohort 75.2% accuracy (95% CI 71.4–77.1%); no-pain-vs-pain classification SVM 75.6% (95% CI 71.9–77.6%). dPLI/PE/peak frequency significant individually; wPLI excluded, so no wPLI metric.
items.prediction_target: Baseline versus cold-pressor-task EEG condition (separately in control and chronic-pain adolescents); no-pain vs pain group-label result is also reported.
items.validation_design: 19-channel EEG, 10-s epochs, SVM/logistic models; paper reports test/train performance. External validation not verified.
items.data_url: Not provided as a repository link
items.data_evidence: Article data-availability statement says raw supporting data ‘will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation’; no public repository link verified.
items.relevance_limitations: Adolescent cold-pressor paradigm and 10-s epochs differ from 5-s chronic adult signals. wPLI was removed from classifier; reported accuracy does not evidence wPLI prediction. Task condition confounds subjective pain; no repository link and data are on request.

items.title: Brain dysfunction in chronic pain patients assessed by resting-state electroencephalography
items.feature_family: Phase-based functional connectivity: PLV and dwPLI; amplitude-envelope correlation comparator
items.feature_definition: Sensor-pair connectivity estimated from phase synchrony (PLV/dwPLI); chronic pain resting-state EEG compared with healthy controls.
items.prediction_rationale: Reported pain-control connectivity differences can motivate a participant-level group classifier, but sensitivity/specificity and clinical validity need independent validation.
items.verified_result_metric: SVM patient/control accuracy 57% (above chance as reported); corrected comparisons found increased theta and >60-Hz frontal connectivity. This is classification accuracy, not variance explained.
items.prediction_target: Chronic pain versus healthy-control group; not continuous pain severity
items.validation_design: 101 chronic-pain patients plus healthy controls; resting-state feature comparison and SVM classification. Data/scripts available on request, not a public validation set.
items.data_evidence: Article data-availability statement explicitly says all scripts and data are available on request.
items.relevance_limitations: Important feature-family precedent, but frontal topography is unavailable in C3/C4/Cz; gamma above 64 Hz exceeds 128-Hz Nyquist and >40 Hz is removed by pipeline filter. Do not interpret 57% classification as variance or regression performance.

items.title: Reproducibility of Functional Connectivity and Graph Measures Based on the Phase Lag Index (PLI) and Weighted Phase Lag Index (wPLI) Derived from High Resolution EEG
items.feature_family: PLI/wPLI test-retest reliability and inter-subject variability
items.feature_definition: PLI indexes asymmetry of pairwise instantaneous phase differences; wPLI weights by magnitude of imaginary phase relation; repeated 256-channel eyes-closed resting EEG.
items.prediction_rationale: Reliability statistics can screen candidate phase features for repeatability before pain prediction; reliability is not itself a pain predictor.
items.verified_result_metric: 44 healthy subjects; 35 follow-up participants at years 1/2; global PLI/wPLI ICC 0.68–0.80, regional 0.58–0.77; PLI CoV 0.12–0.28, wPLI CoV 0.25–0.55.
items.prediction_target: Not a pain-prediction target; transferable feature repeatability
items.validation_design: Longitudinal test-retest at baseline and years 1/2; repeated resting-state EEG.
items.data_evidence: Source paper reports repeated EEG sample and metrics, but no public raw-data repository was verified; do not treat published tables as raw EEG.
items.relevance_limitations: Transferable feature-reliability evidence only; healthy cohort and 256-channel montage, not pain. Longitudinal years-scale reliability does not guarantee five-second window stability; only a subset of the 256-channel network is available in current pipeline.

items.title: Reliability and state-dependency of EEG connectivity, complexity and network characteristics
items.feature_family: PLI functional connectivity reliability; complexity and network measures as comparators
items.feature_definition: 64-channel EEG PLI/AECc, entropy and minimum spanning tree metrics across repeated resting sessions and semi-resting task epochs.
items.prediction_rationale: Feature stability across time/state is a necessary screening condition before a connectivity feature is interpreted as pain-related; it is not direct pain prediction evidence.
items.verified_result_metric: n=42 repeated sessions, n=24 semi-rest comparisons; alpha PLI among most robust measures; theta/alpha PE ICC >0.75–0.90; PLI ICC range described as poor-to-excellent overall.
items.validation_design: Two sessions six weeks apart; resting versus semi-rest task; ICC at sensor/source level.
items.data_evidence: Retrieved primary abstract verifies design and findings; no public participant-level EEG repository verified.
items.relevance_limitations: Healthy-adult repeatability is not pain validity. State and task effects may matter for baseline timing; only central channels available; 64-channel network metrics cannot be reconstructed.

items.title: Connectivity Analysis in EEG Data: A Tutorial Review of the State of the Art and Emerging Trends
items.authors: Giovanni Chiarion, Laura Sparacino, Yuri Antonacci, Luca Faes, Luca Mesin
items.feature_family: Phase, coherence, directed, multivariate and information-theoretic EEG connectivity; methodological review
items.feature_definition: Tutorial compares data-driven EEG functional connectivity approaches and their assumptions/limitations, including preprocessing and source-localization impacts.
items.prediction_rationale: Use to choose/interpret phase features and avoid equating functional connectivity with causal communication; no pain prediction is reported.
items.validation_design: Narrative/tutorial methods review; no independent cohort validation.
items.data_evidence: Review article; not a dataset publication and no raw EEG data claim is used here.
items.relevance_limitations: Transferable EEG methods only, not direct pain evidence or a feature-performance benchmark. Connectivity is pairwise statistical dependence, not causal interaction; phase metrics require enough oscillatory cycles and careful artifact/volume-conduction control.

items.title: DISCOVER-EEG: an open, fully automated EEG pipeline for biomarker discovery in clinical neuroscience
items.feature_family: Automated EEG feature pipeline including oscillatory power, connectivity (dwPLI) and network characteristics
items.feature_definition: Open BIDS workflow for resting EEG preprocessing, feature extraction and visualization; includes debiased weighted phase-lag index connectivity.
items.prediction_rationale: Reusable reference for reproducible extraction of phase connectivity; it does not establish a pain prediction model.
items.verified_result_metric: Tested pipeline on openly available LEMON (213 participants) and TDBRAIN (1274 participants) datasets; verifies pipeline capability, not pain prediction accuracy.
items.prediction_target: Not pain; general resting EEG biomarker workflow
items.validation_design: Pipeline demonstrated on two independent publicly available EEG datasets; healthy adults and mainly psychiatric patients.
items.data_url: Not applicable (software item; input datasets are external)
items.data_evidence: Article states pipeline code is on GitHub and co-deposited at Zenodo; states it was tested with two openly available EEG datasets, but this row is a software entry, not a dataset claim.
items.relevance_limitations: Transferable infrastructure, no pain cohort and no pain prediction results. Pipeline setup uses resting-state BIDS data and channel/network coverage beyond current three central leads; does not replace validation of window length or feature stability.

conflicts: The requested ‘2021 resting frontal neuropathic pain PAC paper’ resolves to Ryu et al., Scientific Reports 2024 (published online 30 Aug 2024; DOI 10.1038/s41598-024-71219-3). 2021 search hits point to an IASP commentary/summary, not the article publication year.
Han et al. is an open 2026 article and links an OSF EEG-data page, but the captured OSF endpoint rendered a sign-in page; therefore raw public EEG accessibility remains unverified here.

Bott et al. 2025 reports 614 people and eight datasets gathered with external-group contributions, but this research did not verify a public participant-level data repository; cohort size must not be confused with public access.

Ryu et al.’s R²=0.655 is regression R², whereas Hohn et al.’s 57% and Teel et al.’s 75% are classification accuracy; none is interchangeable with variance coverage or correlation. Ryu’s R² is not externally validated in saved evidence.
gaps: Two unique public pain EEG resources were verified in this phase: Zolezzi et al.’s chronic neuropathic resting EEG dataset (also reanalyzed by Ryu et al.) and Zhao et al.’s laser-evoked EEG dataset. The linked Ryu paper is not a separate dataset.
No verified open raw-EEG dataset was established for the Bott mega-analysis or Teel wearable adolescent study; the latter explicitly offers data on request, which is not public access.

No robust pain EEG validation cohort using PLV/PLI/wPLI/PAC with externally validated continuous pain R²/correlation was verified. Several studies report within-sample state/group classification or candidate associations, not clinical prediction.

For current C3/C4/Cz-only 128-Hz processing, frontal Fp1/Fp2 and frontal-occipital/limbic network claims are not directly testable; >64-Hz high gamma exceeds Nyquist, >40-Hz features are filtered out, and task/event/baseline studies need marker-aligned windows. 5-s epochs may be too short for stable low-frequency phase estimates; validate window-length sensitivity.
